title: PAP Supply Replenishment Program Four-Hour Night Share Following a Practitioner Re-Evaluation
content:
## Questions and answers for the documentation desk

**What share of a download window's nights must reach four hours of use when the patient has been re-evaluated?**
When a compliance download of the patient's PAP device is read as proof of continued use for the PAP Supply Replenishment Program, the share of the window's nights that must reach four hours of use is:

- **40 percent** for a patient with a practitioner re-evaluation documenting benefit dated within the last 12 months;
- **55 percent** for a patient whose newest re-evaluation documenting benefit is older than 12 months.

For a patient with no re-evaluation documenting benefit on the device record, no such re-evaluation share applies.

**Where is the re-evaluation found?** On the patient's device record under PAP Therapy Equipment: a practitioner re-evaluation received that documents benefit, with its visit date. A re-evaluation that does not document benefit is not one of these.

**How is "within the last 12 months" measured?** By whole calendar months from the newest re-evaluation's visit date to the handling day: fewer than 12 whole months is within the last 12 months (40 percent); 12 whole months or more is older (55 percent).

**How is the share applied?** The nights of the window with four or more hours of use, taken as a share of all the nights in the window, must be at least the percentage.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical dates)

| Newest re-evaluation documenting benefit | Handling day | Whole months | Share required |
|---|---|---|---|
| 9 June of the previous year | 8 June | 11 | 40 percent |
| 8 June of the previous year | 8 June | 12 | 55 percent |
| none on the device record | any | — | no re-evaluation share |

## Example (hypothetical)

A window of 30 nights with 14 nights at four hours or more: 14 is about 47 percent of 30. With a re-evaluation documenting benefit 5 months old, the required share is 40 percent and 47 percent meets it. With the newest such re-evaluation 18 months old, the required share is 55 percent and 47 percent falls short.
